texts: Three years sober now, and the cravings still show up every evening, but my sponsor says a true hero is the one who gets knocked down daily and still never walks away from the fight.
fight your own cravings
The true hero is not the one who conquers cities, but the one who wages war on his own cravings and never turns his back.
doha about not running away from the fight with my own anger, ive lost many rounds but im still in it
Please write a doha about the real warrior who fights the war within against lust and anger, who may be wounded a hundred times but never runs from the struggle, and who is therefore called a hero.
hero beats his temper
My father had a ferocious temper all his life, and at sixty he decided to fight it, and every time he felt it rising he walked out and counted, and he has not raised his voice in four years.
doha on conquering my own anger, thats the real fight
Write me a doha for the person who is at war with his own anger every day, saying that the one who keeps fighting it without surrender is a greater hero than any who conquer others.
He who slays his own wrath has slain the fiercest foe; salutes to him who stays and fights.
doha w a bee and a washerman - the washerman fights the stain, the bee fights its own sting, both stay in the fight and dont flee
bee, washerman, stay and fight

Write a doha about the washerman who keeps scrubbing the stains of the mind, standing his ground when a bee buzzes and stings, teaching that the true hero fights his inner war and never flees the field.
The washerman at our ghat once told me that scrubbing out a hard stain is like fighting your own temper, and a bee that had stung him earlier still hovered about, and he did not run.
The bee may sting and the stain may cling, yet the washerman stays; so stays the hero in his inner war.
paras, door, hero stays
At the door of the paras the true hero stands unflinching against lust and anger; he is cut to pieces, yet he leaves not.
I stood at the door of my ex's flat for an hour deciding whether to go in and fall back into the old pattern, then turned around, and my friend said that was the paras of my recovery.
Write a doha about a warrior who stands at the door guarding the paras of the heart against lust and anger, who is wounded but never abandons his post, for he is the true hero.
doha w the paras and a door - hero guards the door of his heart against lust n anger and never leaves
doha for staying strong against temptation, i keep wanting to relapse
Every night at eleven the urge comes to open that old app again, and every night for ninety days I have just stayed in my chair and breathed through it, and I think that is the bravest thing I do.
The brave one stays in the struggle though the craving howls; he is the hero who is not cut down by his own wish.
I need a doha for someone fighting a long battle with an addiction, reminding him that the true hero is the one who keeps standing and never quits the struggle, even if he falls a thousand times.
hold your ground
I'd love a doha about the hero who carries the pot of water on his head through a crowd of temptations, spilling not a drop of his purpose, standing firm in the inner war and never fleeing.
The pot of water on his head, the war in his heart; the true hero walks on and lets nothing be spilled.
doha w a pot of water - hero walks through all the temptations and doesnt spill a drop of his resolve
At the village fair my uncle carried a heavy pot of water on his head through a crowd of men drinking, who shouted at him to join, and he smiled and did not give in.
pot of water, resolve
Write a doha about the mirror that shows the true hero his own faults of lust and anger, and how he does not look away or run but stays to fight them every day until they are conquered.
When I looked in the mirror after losing my temper at my daughter, I saw the thing I hated, and I decided to fight it every day, and last week for the first time I walked away instead of shouting.
In the mirror stands the foe he fears the most, himself; yet the true hero looks and does not flee.
mirror, face your enemy
doha w a mirror - the real enemy is in the mirror, and the hero stays to fight it
paras, gold, hero's fight
My teacher said no paras will turn a person to gold unless he fights his own anger and greed daily, and I have been trying, losing often, but never quitting the practice.
doha w the paras and gold - the real transformation is fighting lust and anger inside, not magic
Write a doha about how the paras and gold are of less worth than the hero who wages the inner war against lust and anger, for he who stays in that fight till the end becomes more precious than gold.
The paras turns iron to gold, but the hero's war turns a man to the Lord; he fights, and does not leave the field.
Not for kings nor kingdoms does the hero fight, but for mastery over his own storms; and till the last breath he does not flee.
doha for someone fighting depression and anger every day, never giving up
Give me a doha for the one who fights a daily war with his own dark moods, rage and desire, wounded again and again yet always returning to the fight, for such a one is the true warrior.
inner war, no retreat
My brother has battled his rage since he was a boy, and each time he loses control he apologises and starts again the next morning, and I realise that this is bravery most people never see.
The chakor keeps its gaze on one distant glow and the pearl waits in the deep; the true hero fights for both and leaves not the field.
doha w a chakor and a pearl - stay in the inner fight and the pearl comes, like the chakor never looks away
Write a doha about the chakor bird that never looks away from its beloved and the pearl won only by the one who dives within, showing that the true hero stays in the inner war until the prize is won.
chakor, pearl, hold the field
My meditation teacher said I would find the pearl within only if I stayed in the fight against my restless desires like a chakor bird that never looks away, and so I sit every dawn and do not quit.
Cleric and cuckoo alike know no hero but the one who fights the war within; call him brave who does not flee.
doha w a cleric and a cuckoo - the cuckoo sings in a fight with its own silence and the cleric fights his desires, both heroes
A cleric in our town admitted that he fights his own anger daily, and that every Friday he sits quietly listening to the cuckoo outside and does not leave until his heart has stopped shaking.
cleric, cuckoo, inner battle
Write a doha about the cleric who fights his lust and anger in secret every day, and the cuckoo that sings through its pain, showing that the true hero is the one who never abandons the inner battle.
never leave the fight
doha: u can lose a hundred times but if u dont run from the fight ur still a hero
My son has failed to control his temper in ten school fights, but each time he goes back and tries again, and his teacher says she has seen few boys with that grit in forty years.

A doha, please, about the true hero who may be defeated a hundred times in the war against his own passions, but who never runs away and returns to fight each morning, therefore he is the one who wins.
A hundred times defeated, still he returns; that is the hero who does not know how to leave.
fight, don't flee
After my husband died I was angry at everyone, at God, at myself, and every day I fought the rage instead of letting it consume me, and slowly I learned to live again.
Please write a Kabir style doha that praises the person who stays and fights the war against lust, anger and greed within himself, who is cut to pieces yet never leaves, and says he alone is a hero.
Better a hundred wounds in the war within than one retreat; the hero is the one who stays.
doha: only the one who fights his own demons and stays is a real hero

Write a doha about an elephant amid a field of war who stands firm though pierced by wounds, and a winnowing fan that sifts the true from the false, showing that the hero holds his ground in the inner battle.
doha w an elephant and winnowing fan - elephant stays in the war even wounded, the fan sifts out the cowards
elephant, winnowing fan, hold firm
My uncle, a retired army man, said the real hero is like the elephant who never moves when the crowd surges, and at harvest he used the winnowing fan and told us that only the steady grain stays.
The elephant stands wounded but does not leave the war; the winnowing fan blows away those who flee, and only the hero remains.
doha w a swan and an arrow - the swan keeps gliding while arrows whiz past, hero stays in the fight
Write a doha in which a swan glides on while an arrow flies past, unmoved, and the hero stands in the inner war against lust and anger, pierced and bleeding but never retreating from the field.
The arrow whistles, the swan glides on; the hero bleeds but does not leave, for his war is within.
When the angry crowd shouted at my sister, she stood calm like a swan, though an arrow of abuse hit her every second, and she said later it took all her inner strength not to hit back or run.
swan, arrow, no retreat

Need a doha about the man who defeats lust and anger inside himself and is therefore more precious than gold, saying that the hero who stays firm in the inner war is rarer than all the gold in the world.
Gold is common, but the hero who conquers his passions and does not leave the field is rare.
doha w gold - the one who beats lust and greed in himself is worth more than gold
hero worth more than gold
My friend turned down a large sum of gold-plated bribes at work three times, fighting the temptation each time, and said the real victory was not the principle but winning against himself.
The bitter gourd soup my grandmother forced me to drink every spring taught me that discipline is a war you fight against your own appetite, and I did not run from it even as a child.
doha w a bitter gourd - hero drinks the bitter cup of self-discipline and doesnt run away
Write a doha about the bitter gourd that is hard to swallow but heals, like the bitter war against one's own craving, teaching that the true hero faces the bitter fight and stays until he wins.
Bitter as the gourd is the war within, yet the hero drinks it to the last and leaves not the field.
bitter gourd, inner war

Write a doha for someone who feels they are losing the fight against lust and anger day after day, telling them that the hero is not one who never falls but one who stays in the fight and never flees.

A former soldier who now counsels addicts told our group that the real battle is not on any border but in the moment you refuse the first drink, and that he never ran from it though he lost many times.
Not the one who never falls but the one who stands again and fights is called the hero.
doha for the hundredth time i failed at my diet but im not quitting the fight
fall, rise, fight on
master your anger
Could you do a doha about the greatest victory which is not over other people but over one's own anger and desire, won by the person who never leaves the fight within himself till the end.
Many conquer worlds, few conquer themselves; he who does and stays is the true hero.
My boss used to explode at everyone, and one day he said he had decided to fight his temper like an enemy, and for a year now he has been calm, and we respect him far more than before.
doha on winning the fight against my own temper
My grandfather kept a parrot that repeated his old curses, and each time it spoke them he winced and decided afresh to fight the anger that had once been his, and in old age he became gentle.
parrot, fight your anger

Write a doha about the hero who hears his old angry words repeated by a parrot and takes up the fight against his anger once more without fleeing, teaching that a true warrior keeps fighting the inner foe.
doha w a parrot repeating my old angry words, the hero stays and fights his anger
The parrot repeats thy old rage; stand and fight it, hero, for the war is within and the field is thine.

Write a doha about the pearl hidden in the deep, found only by the hero who has fought off lust and anger within and stays steady, never running from the inner war, for he alone is worthy of the pearl.
After many years of fighting my anger and the urge to quit, I began to feel a stillness like a pearl growing in me, and my teacher said it is given only to those who stayed in the fight.
doha w a pearl - only the one who fights his inner enemies and stays gets the pearl
pearl for the steadfast
The pearl is for the hero who wages his inner war and leaves not the field.
doha w sandalwood and a net - the sandalwood stays cool no matter what, and the hero is caught in no net of anger or lust, he stays in the fight
The sandalwood stays cool in the heat of hate; the hero is caught in no net of lust and stays on the field.
sandalwood, net, stay calm
Every day at work my colleagues try to catch me in the net of office gossip and anger, but I remain calm and cool like sandalwood and keep fighting my own temper, and I do not leave the post.
Write a doha about the sandalwood that stays cool though poison coils around it, and the net of desire that cannot catch the true hero, who never leaves the inner war against lust and anger.
moon, steady hero
doha w the moon: hero stays steady in his inner fight like the moon in the night sky

Write a doha about the moon that holds its place in the night sky through every storm, like the hero who stays on the field of the inner war against lust and anger and never flees, however fierce the night.
On the night I nearly gave in to the old habit, I sat on the roof looking at the moon until dawn, and I stayed there with the fight inside me, and by morning I had won.
The moon keeps its place through the storm; the hero keeps his post in the war within.

Write a doha about the crow that flees at the first alarm while the hero stays and fights his inner foes of lust and anger, wounded but not retreating, teaching that cowardice runs and the brave remain.
crow flees, hero stays
doha w a crow - crow flies at the first sign of trouble but the hero stays and fights his lust n anger
The crow flies off at the first noise; the hero stays in the war within and will not run.
My cousin quits everything the moment it gets hard, like a crow startled by a noise, while his sister has battled her temper for years and never given up, and the family knows who the brave one is.
doha w a lotus - hero lives in the mud of desires but doesnt flee, fights it every day
A lotus pond near our school stays clean though muddy, and my teacher said the person who fights anger and lust within him is like that, always in the mud and always winning, and never leaving.
I'd love a doha about the lotus that stays in the mud and still blooms untouched, like the hero who stays in the thick of lust and anger without fleeing and wins his inner war.
The lotus stays in the mud and is not stained; the hero stays in the war and is not conquered.
lotus in the mud
Let the fire of anger and the dew of calm contend in his heart; the hero holds the field until the dew prevails.
When the fire of rage rises in me, I stand in the garden at dawn and watch the dew on the grass, and I do not leave until it settles, and that is how I fight my temper.
doha w fire and dew - fire of anger vs dew of calm in me, and the hero stays in the fight until the dew wins
fire, dew, inner contest
Write a doha about the hero in whose heart the fire of lust and anger fights with the cool dew of patience, who stays on the field through the entire struggle until the dew wins, never fleeing.
Walking across the desert sand under the hot sun, I wanted to give up a hundred times, and each time I told myself this was the same fight as the one with my anger, and I reached the village.
On the hot sand under the sun he walks, and the fight within is greater than the heat; the hero does not turn back.
sand, sun, no retreat

Write a doha about a hero who stays on the field under the burning sun and hot sand, fighting his inner foes of lust and anger and never fleeing, wounded though he is, because retreat is not in his nature.
doha w sand and the sun - hero doesnt run from the sun-baked battle within, he fights it out
At my uncle's bier all the family quarrelled about the will, and my aunt, who bit her tongue the whole day instead of joining the shouting, was the one real hero among us.
doha w a bier and a tongue - hero bites his tongue and doesnt fight with words at the bier, wins the inner war
bier, tongue, self-control

Give me a doha about the hero who stands at the bier amid quarrelling relatives and holds back his sharp tongue, winning the war against his anger and never fleeing his post, for that is the greatest victory.
By the bier of the dead, the angry tongue is stilled by the hero who fights wrath within and stays.
Write a doha about the hero who goes down into the well of his own heart to fight the lust and anger that lurk at its bottom, and who does not climb out until they are conquered.
well, descend and fight
He descends into the well of his own heart to face the beasts below, and does not climb back out till they are slain.
When my meditation went deep I felt like I was descending a water well into the dark, where all my old anger lived, and I did not turn back, I stayed and fought it.
doha w a well - the hero goes down into the well of his heart and fights what's there
hold the line
When temptation and rage rise together, he plants his feet and fights; the hero knows no other course.
doha for the moments when i want to give in and give up on my self-control
Last Tuesday I was so angry at my sister that I wanted to say the cruellest thing I knew, so I locked myself in the bathroom for twenty minutes and breathed, and came out and said nothing.

A doha, please, for the moment of great temptation when the mind says give up, telling the seeker that the hero is the one who stands his ground against desire and rage and does not flee the inner war.
In the house of the heart rages the war; the hero guards it, and at no turn does he leave his post.
doha w a house - the hero defends his own house, i mean his heart, from lust and anger and never leaves
house of the heart
Write a doha about the hero who defends the house of his heart against the invaders lust and anger, who is wounded in every room but does not abandon his house, for he is the true warrior.
After my father's death I moved back into the old house and fought every night against the urge to drink, and the house seemed to hold me up, and I did not leave, and the urge finally faded.
My aunt told me that when she sews she thinks of the thread of her anger and keeps cutting it, and she goes back to her sewing each day to fight the same temper, never walking out on the struggle.
Write a doha about the hero who keeps cutting the thread of lust and anger that binds him, stitching his resolve again every time it is torn, never leaving the field, so that at last he is free.
thread of anger
doha w a thread - keep cutting the thread of anger and starting again, the hero never leaves
He cuts the thread of rage, again and again; the hero is he who does not tire of the cutting.
Lust and anger are two armies that besiege the heart; the hero stands alone against both, and flees not.

I joined a men's group for anger management and the first thing the leader said was that this is the hardest war you will ever fight, and you will lose daily, and the only unforgivable thing is to leave.
hold the heart
doha: the real war is inside, and the hero is one who never leaves it

Need a doha about two armies, lust and anger, that attack the heart of a man, and about the hero who stands alone against both without retreating, wounded but unconquered, because the inner war is the only one that matters.
stay in the fight
He is cut to pieces, piece by piece, and still he does not leave; this is the true hero.
Please write a doha about a hero who is cut to pieces in the war against his own lust and anger, yet will not leave the field, so that his steadfastness marks him out as the true warrior.
My therapist told me healing from a bad past is a battle you will lose every day for a year, and the only difference between hero and coward is that one keeps coming back to the session.
doha: even if i lose every day, the hero doesnt leave
doha about not running away from my problems and my temper, i want to be the one who stays
Write a doha for a young man who has always run away whenever the fight with his own anger and cravings got too hard, urging him to be the hero who stays and fights until the end.

Whenever my father shouted at us, my brother would leave the flat for days, but this time he stayed and answered quietly, and my father broke down, and I think my brother fought a harder war that night.
stay, don't run
The coward flees his own heart's war; the hero stays, though cut in a hundred pieces, and wins.

Could you do a doha about the real meaning of heroism, which is not defeating an outer enemy but remaining steadfast in the war against one's own lust, anger and greed, wounded and never turning away from the field.
The warrior of the outer field is praised, but the warrior of the heart is the greater; he stays and fights.
My father, a decorated soldier, told me on his deathbed that the toughest enemy he faced was not on any border but in his own mind, and that he never ran from that fight either.
doha about heroism being about conquering yourself, not others
the greater hero
At sixteen I was caught up in a gang and every day I had to fight the urge to hit back, and my mentor taught me the strongest man in the room is the one who doesn't hit.
strength is restraint
doha on being brave enough to not hit back, real strength is self control
The raised fist is easy; the lowered fist is the labour of the hero who wars with his wrath.
Write a doha for a young man tempted by violence, telling him that the real warrior fights his own wrath and never flees the struggle, and that holding back his hand is a greater feat than any blow.
The seed of anger the hero sifts in the winnowing fan of patience; he stays through the winnowing till the husk is gone.
I plant a seed every time I fight my anger and win, in a small planter by my window, and my aunt, who winnows the grain in the courtyard, says the hero keeps at it until the harvest of peace.
Write a doha about the hero who sifts the seed of his anger in the winnowing fan of patience, staying through the long labour of the inner war until all the husk of lust and wrath is blown away.
seed, winnowing fan, inner fight
doha w a seed and a winnowing fan - the hero sifts out anger and lust from his heart and doesnt quit

Please give me a couplet for a person fighting depression, loneliness and bitter urges for many years, saying that the one who stands up each morning and fights is a true hero, though the world never sees his war.
No applause sounds for the hero of the heart, yet he fights each dawn and leaves not; the world knows not his war.
doha for ppl fighting mental health battles quietly, they are heroes
quiet inner hero
My mother has fought a quiet battle with sadness since I was a child, and each morning she gets up and cooks for us anyway, and I have realised that this is the bravest thing I have seen.
On the mountain of the self the hero keeps the house of the heart, and flees not though the siege be long.

My grandfather's old house on the mountain was attacked by storms and landslides every year, and he stayed and fought to keep it standing, and he said that is how you hold the house of your heart too.
doha w a mountain and a house - hero holds the house on the mountain against everything, no retreat
house on the mountain
Write a doha about the hero who climbs the mountain of his own self to defend the house of the heart from lust and anger, who is wounded but never leaves his post, and so is crowned the true warrior.
lock, shroud, fight on
Write a doha about the hero who keeps the lock on the heart against lust and anger, and who fights the inner war not till the day he is tired, but till the shroud is laid upon him, never fleeing.
My grandmother kept a heavy lock on her heart against anger all her life, sewn into her shroud at the end, and she fought her temper till her last day, and the whole family says she died a hero.
doha w a lock and a shroud - hero keeps the lock on his heart and fights lust till he's in the shroud
The lock of the heart he guards, and the shroud he fears not; the hero fights on till the shroud is laid upon him.
peacock, cleric, steadfast
doha w a peacock and a cleric - peacock stays proud in the storm, the cleric stays in his inner fight, both dont run

I'd love a doha about the peacock that spreads its feathers undaunted in the storm and the cleric who stays firm in the war against his own anger, both showing that the hero stands his ground and never flees.
The peacock dances through the storm and the cleric fights through the night; neither deserts the field of the heart.

In our town the cleric's long fight against his own anger was known to all, and the peacock that came to his courtyard each morning seemed to watch him with respect, as he stayed to the end of every struggle.
The shadow of lust follows and the shadow of wrath stands before; yet the hero turns not, and fights them both.
shadow, stand and fight
doha w a shadow - hero fights his shadow, the dark side, and stays until the end
I used to run from my own shadow, from the part of me that grew angry and cruel, but my counselor taught me to turn around and look at it and fight it, and I finally stopped running.
Write a doha about the hero who turns to face the dark shadow of lust and anger within him, rather than running from it, and who fights it on his own ground until he is free, never leaving the field.
stone-hearted hero
The stone feels not the blow, nor the hero the sting of his craving; he stands, and it is the craving that breaks.
doha w a stone - hero is steady like a stone, doesnt flee his inner war

When my boss shouted at the whole team, my colleague stood there like a stone, calm and unmoved, and afterwards he told me he had spent ten years training himself to never flee a fight and never start one.
Write a doha about the hero who stands as steady as a stone against the waves of lust and anger within him, who is struck again and again but does not move, and who therefore wins the inner war.
The date palm bends in the storm and rises, rooted deep; so the hero, bent by passion, stays on the field.
date palm, rooted
The date palm in our courtyard has survived forty storms by bending and never leaving the ground, and my father says that is how he fights his own temper, bending but not running.
Give me a doha about the date palm that bends in the storm yet stays rooted to its ground, like the hero in the inner war against lust and anger who is bent by every blow but never leaves.
doha w a date palm - bends in every storm but stays rooted, hero in his inner war
jaggery, shroud, to the end

Write a doha about the hero tempted by sweet jaggery of desire at every step yet refusing it, fighting the war within until the shroud is laid on him, never fleeing, so that he is called the greatest warrior.
doha w jaggery and a shroud - hero refuses sweet temptation jaggery and fights till the shroud

My diabetic grandfather refused jaggery and every sweet offered to him for his last twenty years, a daily war against craving, and he was buried in a plain shroud with a smile, and we called him a hero.
Jaggery tempts him all his life and he stays at the post; at last the shroud is laid on a hero.
Write a doha about the river of desire that surges against the hero who stands firm on its bank, fighting lust and anger within, who is washed by waves of temptation but never leaves his post.
Every evening by the river my uncle faced the old urge to drink, standing there until it passed, and the river flowed on, and he said he learned to be like the bank, not leaving.
The river of desire roars and the hero stands on the bank; the waters pass, but he remains.
doha w a river - the river of desire flows hard and the hero doesnt budge from the bank
river of desire, firm bank

Please write a doha for the person who is fighting for his marriage, calming his anger and holding back his desires, who has chosen not to leave the struggle, calling him the true hero of the household.
He fights not abroad but at his own table; the hero of the household is he who vanquishes himself.
My husband and I almost split twice, and each time one of us chose to stay and swallow our pride and anger, and I think of those moments as quiet battles where we both stayed.
doha for a man trying to save his marriage by controlling his temper
control, don't leave

A doha, please, about the great hero who fights alone against anger and lust for a whole lifetime, with no witnesses and no medals, yet does not flee the field, showing that real heroism is hidden and silent.
My grandmother never raised her voice in sixty years of marriage to a difficult man, a lifelong war she fought in silence, and at her funeral the elder called her the bravest person he had known.
unseen hero
doha about silent heroes who fight their anger and urges and no one knows
No bard will sing the war he fought, no honour mark his field; yet the hero of the heart stood to the end.
skeleton, still standing
After forty years of fighting alcoholism, my uncle looked like a skeleton, but he stood tall at his sobriety anniversary, and everyone clapped for a man who never left the field.
Though the war has left him a skeleton, bare and bone, the hero stands on the field; he never fled his inner war.
Write a doha about the old hero reduced to a skeleton by a lifetime of war against lust and anger, who yet stands firm on the field and has never fled, and is more alive than the cowards who ran.
doha w a skeleton - after years of fighting lust and anger hes just a skeleton but still standing
